brief: Stands in for a language-model port in tests, replaying seeded answers and counting calls, with no model and no network.
detail: A port is any object with a Complete method that answers a hash list with ok, text and from. This one gives three things a real model cannot: determinism (a seeded prompt always gets the same answer), a measurable cost (the number of calls and an approximate token count, so a budget becomes an assertion) and offline use. A seeded answer is tried first, then a fragment rule, then the fallback; in strict mode, the default, anything else raises an error. It cannot reproduce the quality of a real model: use it for the shape of a pipeline, prompts assembled and answers parsed, and judge quality against the real thing separately. Its state lives in a shared table, so a copy of the object sees the same answers and calls.
